operator_reported_not_independently_obse: An Escape cancellation and one mixed-input pass were reported as performed on the rail search. The retained end state showed only the committed 日本語, so the intermediate preedit and the cancelled text are not independently observed and are recorded as NOT_MEASURED.
The Operator reported no duplicate insertion in any step; duplicate absence is independently supported only by ax1-n2, ax1-n3 and ax1-n5's observed values.

defect_and_fix.defect: The Task Rail search UIA TextInput node exposed no value property, while the palette and flow inputs exposed theirs, so the rail query could not be read from the accessibility tree. Whether a screen reader announces the field correctly, and whether IME preedit (unconfirmed) text would be exposed once a value exists, are NOT_MEASURED.
defect_and_fix.evidence: ax1-n1 and ax1-n2 (the rail node carried no value before the fix) against the flow surface's exposed value in ax1-n3, and the post-fix rail values in ax1-n4 and ax1-n5
defect_and_fix.fix: crates/desktop-gpui/src/lib.rs: added .aria_value(SharedString::from(query_text.clone())) to the task-search element, using the raw query rather than the caret-decorated display string
defect_and_fix.scope: one attribute on one element; no new API, dependency, unsafe/FFI, TSF/COM work, token or contract change
defect_and_fix.regression_coverage: no unit test was added: the observable is produced by the accessibility bridge, and a source-text assertion would be tautological. The independent reproduction is the Native before/after pair ax1-n1/ax1-n4 and ax1-n2/ax1-n5.
defect_and_fix.not_claimed: this is not a screen-reader product acceptance and does not close DC-MP-AX1's screen-reader scope

gate_environment_qualification.status: RESOLVED by an explicit, isolated check environment (final state)
retained_checkout_experiments: with RUSTC_WRAPPER empty and a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR/CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings completed in 8.4 s with exit 0

cargo test -p ui-model --no-run failed with "linker link.exe not found": the host's MSVC link.exe lives in a Visual Studio 2019 BuildTools tree and is reachable only through the ambient PATH, which Refine reserves and does not pass
supplying CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_PC_WINDOWS_MSVC_LINKER and LIB (MSVC 14.29.30133 lib/x64 plus Windows Kits 10.0.19041.0 ucrt/um) linked the ui-model test binary successfully in 19.2 s

with that linker plus MSVC env, clippy then failed inside a cc-rs C++ build script (vswhom-sys ext/vswhom.cpp): cl.exe exists but cannot resolve its dependent DLLs without the Visual Studio developer environment on PATH
the bundled rust-lld alternative cannot link either: rust-lld reports 'could not open msvcrt.lib', and no msvcrt.lib copy exists outside the MSVC BuildTools lib directory
gate_environment_qualification.conclusion: HISTORICAL (attempts 1-2, superseded): the independent Gate could not execute this project's linking/build checks in the minimal child environment. Attempt 1 failed on cargo resolution and attempt 2 on the compiler-cache panic; the retained-checkout experiments then showed that clippy and linking work once the MSVC linker, LIB, CC/CXX/AR and INCLUDE are supplied.
gate_environment_qualification.decision_needed: SUPERSEDED by the third execution, which ran with an explicit environment but pointed CARGO_TARGET_DIR at the repository's development target. The storage boundary requires Refine's fresh external check targets to stay separate from the ordinary development target and forbids sharing mutable targets between independent checks, so gate 91a15539 is NOT policy-compliant and cannot be counted as an independent verification. The remaining decision is a compliant re-run: a fresh external target per Gate plus an approved content-addressed compiler cache (with an explicit cache directory) to stay inside the 600 s cap, or a Caller-approved alternative.
resolution: the operator's cargo configuration routes rustc through a compiler cache whose Windows configuration lookup fails under Refine's private HOME; the checks therefore set RUSTC_WRAPPER empty and CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS empty so the cached per-target -fuse-ld flag is not passed to a linker that does not support it

the checks name the operator CARGO_HOME and RUSTUP_HOME so the pinned toolchain is reused, and a repository-local CARGO_TARGET_DIR so independent checks reuse built dependencies instead of rebuilding them
the MSVC linker is named explicitly through the target linker variable, with LIB pointing at the VS 2019 BuildTools 14.29.30133 x64 libraries plus Windows Kits 10.0.19041.0 ucrt/um

the C/C++ toolchain for build scripts is supplied with target-specific CC/CXX/AR variables and INCLUDE pointing at the MSVC include tree plus Windows Kits 10.0.19041.0 ucrt/shared/um include trees; the earlier failure was an INCLUDE set built from Lib instead of Include paths
PATH is still not passed; every tool is reached through an absolute configured path or an explicit variable

a fourth attempt with the compiler cache and an explicit cache directory still failed on the cache's configuration lookup, so the final Gate disables the cache and pays a cold compile inside its own fresh target; measured cost stayed inside the 600 s cap
gate_environment_qualification.isolation_violation: gate 91a15539 reused the repository development target through CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so its five checks did not run against fresh external targets; the closure is therefore recorded as an executed Gate with a non-compliant build area rather than as an independent verification result
